title: Zoomable bandline + anchored tooltip semantics for high-density time-series (keyboard-first a11y)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: dense time-series charts (e.g., 5k+ points, variable sampling) currently lose actionable context when users zoom and when keyboard users or screen reader users try to inspect series. Existing tooltip anchoring is mouse-centric (nearest-x) and creates flicker during continuous panning/zoom. Bandline visualization (min/median/max ribbon) exists but is disconnected from tooltip/keyboard focus semantics.

Goal: introduce a bandline rendering mode with explicit anchored tooltip semantics that: 1) keeps keyboard-first focus stable as users pan/zoom; 2) reduces redraw and layout churn for performance on lower-tier GPUs; 3) exposes accessible labels/announcements for SR users; 4) uses design tokens for band color/alpha and tooltip spacing to match system theming.

Scope: design interaction states, keyboard focus model, SR announcements, tooltip anchor rules, fallback (canvas vs SVG), and token mapping for bandline and tooltip spacing. Engineering work (rendering, caching, kernel hints) will be tracked in ENG subtasks.
acceptance_criteria: Bandline rendering mode added to chart component with token-driven colors (band-fill, band-border, median-line).
Tooltip anchor modes: mouse (closest point), keyboard (explicit anchor by focus index), and pinned (user toggled) documented and available in stories.

Keyboard navigation: left/right arrow moves focus by sample/index for focused series; Home/End jump to viewport bounds; focus ring visible and announced by SR: "Focused series <name>, value <value>, range <min>-<max>".
Zoom/pan interactions keep anchor stable: when focus is on an index, panning preserves that index if still in-range; otherwise nearest-in-view behavior defined and documented.

Performance: interactive pan/zoom at 60fps on reference medium machine (measured in ENG perf harness) for up to 3 concurrent series with density up to 4k points using canvas path + bandline decimation fallback.
Design tokens: all colors, alphas, spacing, and tooltip offsets mapped to design token names and added to token docs.
Figma spec and component stories (Chromatic) with keyboard and SR simulated states are published and linked.
Docs: migration notes for existing charts with bandline opt-in flag and recommended defaults for desktop/mobile.
decisions: Use canvas-based draw pipeline for primary renderer and SVG fallback only for low-density or when annotation interactivity requires DOM nodes.
Introduce two anchor primitives: index-anchor (keyboard/pinned) and nearest-anchor (mouse), with clear API parameter anchorMode: 'index' | 'nearest' | 'pinned'.
Accessibility announcements will be string templates defined in localization files: e.g., "Series {seriesName}, value {value}, min {min}, max {max}". Screen reader behavior documented in Confluence.
Expose bandline as an opt-in prop initially to reduce breaking changes; default chart behavior unchanged until rollout completes.
tradeoffs: Canvas primary renderer provides best perf but complicates per-point DOM interactions (tooltips/aria). We mitigate with a lightweight hitmap layer that only exposes focused index to assistive tech.
Opt-in rollout slows adoption but avoids regressions for existing customers heavily relying on current tooltip semantics.
Keeping stable-anchor semantics during pan may hide live updates for streaming data; recommended pattern is to offer a "follow live" toggle for streaming charts.
